title: Former Costa Mesa Police Officer Pleads Guilty to Contacting His Mistress Thousands of Times Through Text, Phone Calls, and Social Media Messages, Including More than 100 Times in a Day, Illegally Accessing Confidential Law Enforcement Databases to Track Romantic Rivals, Ex-girlfriend, and Wife

reports.title: Former Costa Mesa Police Officer Pleads Guilty to Contacting His Mistress Thousands of Times Through Text, Phone Calls, and Social Media Messages, Including More than 100 Times in a Day, Illegally Accessing Confidential Law Enforcement Databases to Track Romantic Rivals, Ex-girlfriend, and Wife

summary:
Former Costa Mesa police officer Robert Jay Josett, 35, pleaded guilty to three misdemeanors after harassing a former mistress. Over nine months he contacted her thousands of times by text, phone, and social media, sometimes more than 100 times in one day, and called her and her new boyfriend up to 58 times daily. He also made 13 unauthorized searches in a state law enforcement database to track the woman, a romantic rival, and his own wife, and used a license plate reader system to locate vehicles, including after he was placed on leave.

In June 2024 he was served with a restraining order and notice of termination, then drove by the woman's home and was arrested. Josett was sentenced to three years informal probation and a 52-week domestic violence program, and he had already spent nine months on a GPS ankle monitor. His law enforcement certification review with California's Peace Officers Standards and Training is pending.
